newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Samsung, Fokker talks next week - Dutch.
newsitem.headline: Samsung, Fokker talks next week - Dutch.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Thursday it was optimistic that talks between South Korea's Samsung Aerospace and Fokker, aimed at rescuing the stricken Dutch planemaker, could start next week.

"I'm a little more optimistic that talks (between Fokker and Samsung) can start, but that does not mean the result will be successful," Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers said in a brief statement.
Asked when the talks might start, a spokesman for Wijers told reporters: "Probably next week."
Wijers had been scheduled to brief reporters on a business plan for Fokker, delivered by Samsung to the Dutch government, a Fokker minority shareholder, earlier this week.
He cancelled his appearance at the last minute. A spokesman said the minister was too busy, but had prepared the short statement.
Samsung tabled a concrete proposal for relaunching Fokker on Tuesday, handing over a business plan to the economics ministry.
Samsung is asking The Hague to take a minority stake in a new Fokker and provide large sums of money in subsidies.
Fokker collapsed under a mountain of debt and went bankrupt in March, two months after German parent Daimler Benz Aerospace cut a vital cash lifeline.
The firm has since been kept alive artificially by court-appointed receivers.
The South Koreans are known to be keen to develop a new, bigger, plane, capable of carrying more passengers than Fokker's current line of 50-, 70- and 100-seater jets.
Fokker estimates the development costs of a new 125-seater aircraft at roughly 700 million guilders ($409.1 million).

Talks between Samsung and the Dutch government will focus on new aircraft development credit as the Dutch state will be asked to contribute 30-50 percent of this facility while Samsung and parts suppliers will chip in the rest.
